Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · School & learning

question noun

something asked

also ask a question, answer my question, what a question!

classical

Cic. Fam. 1.9.7
Plin. Ep. 1.5.7: interrogātiō īnsidiōsa (Lewis & Short)

interrogātiō, interrogātiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a question, a questioning

In conversation Latin usually puts the question in the verb, rogāre or interrogāre aliquem aliquid, and “my question” is quod rogō.

Other words

  • quod rogō — what I am asking, my question

    phrase: relative clause with rogō or interrogō · also used · classical · Plaut. Men. 914c: dīc mihi hoc quod tē rogō; Ter. And. 762–764

  • Rogās? — What a question! Need you ask?

    also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 574: Rogās? vidērem, audīrem, essem ūnā quācum cupiēbam; Traupman 89

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.)

    Also Mēn' rogās? (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Tibi ego dīcō, annōn? … Mitte id quod sciō: dīc quod rogō.

    I’m talking to you, aren’t I? … Never mind what I know; answer my question.Ter. And. 762–764

  • dīc mihi hoc quod tē rogō: album an ātrum vīnum pōtās?

    tell me what I’m asking you: do you drink white wine or red?Plaut. Men. 914c

  • Quae interrogātiō, vesperī facta, Pȳthagorēōrum est

    That question, asked in the evening, is the Pythagoreans’Libellus I, Iter in Lūsitāniam

See also ask, question, why.
